title: About
text:
Why Data Science
After being out of school for so long, I really didn’t want to go back to school for 2 years, but I wanted to get a formal education in Data Science. UBC’s MDS program is an accelerated, fast-paced program which you can complete in 10 months, this really drew me towards this program.

title: About
text:
Outside of Data
As I’ve gotten older and had the chance to travel to different cities, I’ve come to appreciate just how lucky I am to have grown up in Vancouver. Having mountains, lakes, and nature so close by has made me want to spend more of my free time outdoors. These days, you’ll often find me hiking, snowboarding, or paddleboarding, depending on the season.
One of the biggest additions to my life has been pickleball. I started playing in 2025, and what began as a casual hobby quickly became something I genuinely look forward to. I enjoy the competitive side of the sport, but I also love the social aspect and the people I’ve met through it.
When I’m not outside or on the pickleball court, I’ve always had video games as another way to spend my time. I regularly play competitive games like League of Legends and Counter-Strike 2, although I enjoy single-player games as well. I’ve always been drawn to competitive games because I enjoy the challenge of improving, learning from mistakes, and pushing myself to get better.

title: Jared Chuang
text:
Hi, my name is Jared Chuang. I’ve been living in Vancouver my whole life, after graduating with a BSc in Mathematics and a diploma in Data Science. I have been working as a Machine Learning Engineer for 2 years. I am hoping to improve upon my skills to hopefully become a Data Engineer.
Outside of professional career, some of my hobbies include hiking, playing video games, and playing pickleball.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Orientation day on campus.


What I thought would be a nightmare to adjust to is going surprisingly well. I have met a lot of new people and even made some new friends. Balancing schoolwork, studying, and my social life has not been too bad. I am able to take notes, listen to all the lectures, and complete labs usually on the same day, allowing me to spend the rest of my day reading ahead or going out to do other things I enjoy. Hopefully, I can keep it that way.
After entering the workforce and going back to school, it feels kind of refreshing to be in a cohort of peers who are all going through the same things together. We’re all going to experience ups and downs together throughout these 10 months.
What I am worried about is whether I will still be able to keep up this routine once the course material gets harder.
